title: POC model triage & bench plan - Skyline Therapeutics
summary: Kickoff for a Q3 POC to shortlist open models for extraction and summarization on clinical notes. Focus: measurable extraction F1, hallucination control, multilingual support (EN/ES/PT), and deployment options that meet data residency and KMS needs. Agreed Redwood will run a 2-week benchmark across several model/config combos once Skyline provides anonymized dataset.
action_items: Aisha: provide ~500 anonymized docs + 50 annotated gold responses by 2026-08-04
Samir: send SOC2 questionnaire and KMS requirements by 2026-07-30
Jared: share Redwood benchmark plan and pricing by 2026-07-31
Priya: prepare perf harness and synthetic traffic scripts by 2026-08-03
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-week benchmark after dataset receipt
Schedule infra deep-dive to validate VPC/KMS options (Marco + Evan)
Follow-up meeting 2026-08-06 to review bench results and pick POC model
transcript:
00:00 Jared Morales: hey everyone thanks for joining, im Jared from Redwood; quick intros?
00:07 Aisha Kapoor: Aisha here, head of ML at Skyline Therapeutics, we run clinical ingestion pipelines.
00:11 Marco Diaz: Marco, infra, i look after network and cost.
00:14 Hannah Lee: Hannah, product lead on this feature.
00:17 Samir Patel: Samir, security.
00:20 Jared Morales: Priya and Evan with me from solutions, Priya will lead bench plan and metrics, Evan on deployment mapping.
00:29 Priya Nair: agenda: define success criteria for extraction and summarization, get workload numbers, propose dataset & bench protocol, and shortlist open models with tradeoffs.
00:41 Aisha Kapoor: context: mix of english (majority) and about 12 percent spanish plus some portuguese. tasks: entity extraction (medications, dosages), relation extraction (adverse events), and long-form summarization for care teams. accuracy for extraction is critical.
00:59 Hannah Lee: timeline: aim for pilot in Q3, 4-week pilot with 2-week blind evaluation then 2-week integration.
01:07 Priya Nair: suggested gating metrics: extraction F1 >= 0.85 on gold, false positive rate < 8 percent; summarization ROUGE-L relative >= 0.6 and human pref > 55 percent. latency targets: p95 < 300ms for 512 tokens on dedicated, p95 < 200ms possible with tuned infra.
01:34 Marco Diaz: traffic: steady 18 requests/sec peak 60 rps bursts. extraction queries ~240 tokens avg, summarization jobs up to 1k tokens and batched. concurrency target 100 sessions.
01:50 Evan Cole: bench plan: 1 hour synthetic peak replay at 60 rps and an 8-hour steady replay at 18 rps, capture p50/p95/p99, GPU util, and token cost.
02:05 Aisha Kapoor: dataset: we can anonymize and share 500 documents plus 50 annotated examples, is that enough?
02:12 Priya Nair: ok for triage; we prefer several hundred annotated examples long term but 50 gold +500 raw is fine to start. we'll run automatic metrics and human review.
02:26 Hannah Lee: for multilingual traffic, should we test single multilingual model or language-specific models?
02:33 Priya Nair: tradeoff: single multilingual simplifies infra but may slightly underperform on rare domain tokens in spanish/pt. recommend starting with a strong multilingual and add language-specific fallback for spanish if needed.
02:48 Jared Morales: model candidates?
02:52 Priya Nair: shortlist families: Mistral-instruct style for speed and reasoning, Llama-2/3 chat-like for instruction, quantized 70B variants for cost savings, and med-adapted smaller models for domain accuracy.
03:10 Evan Cole: concrete bench targets: run community equivalents of Mistral-Instruct-1.1, Llama-2-chat-70B or nearest, quantized 70B with Redwood q4 kernels, and a 13B med-adapted model. capture hallucination stats on extraction and summary tasks.
03:32 Samir Patel: security: we need to ensure anonymized PHI never leaves the VPC unencrypted, and KMS integration is mandatory for hosted POC.
03:40 Jared Morales: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and private deployment; we'll provide SOC2 and KMS docs.
03:47 Marco Diaz: logging: need token-level billing and per-route latency traces.
03:51 Priya Nair: Redwood Console provides per-route token/latency breakdowns and tracing hooks; we can forward logs to Splunk/Datadog.
03:59 Aisha Kapoor: extraction must be prioritized even if summarization lags.
04:04 Hannah Lee: agreed.
04:08 Jared Morales: timeline recap: Redwood will provide a benchmark plan within 48 hours of this call (by 2026-07-31), start runs after dataset arrives, run 7 model/config combos across two weeks, and deliver a comparison deck.
04:25 Aisha Kapoor: 7 model runs is fine.
04:29 Evan Cole: 7 runs are mix of families and config variants (quantized vs fp16) plus the med-adapted 13B.
04:40 Marco Diaz: integration: we want canary A/B against our rule-based extractor and automatic fallback on low confidence.
04:48 Priya Nair: Redwood supports canary + fallback policies; we'll include sample routing rules.
04:56 Samir Patel: need a shared responsibility matrix for logs and key ownership.
05:00 Jared Morales: we'll share a responsibility matrix and KMS patterns including BYOK and HSM options for private.
05:09 Priya Nair: quantization note: rare biomedical tokens can be impacted; we'll benchmark rare-token subsets to measure FP/FN change.
05:18 Evan Cole: long contexts and KV cache size affect memory and tail latency; we'll monitor p99 and memory metrics.
05:28 Hannah Lee: rough cost delta hosted vs dedicated vs private?
05:32 Jared Morales: hosted has higher per-token but no ops; dedicated can cut unit compute cost ~30-45% at commit; private adds platform fee but similar compute economics to dedicated. we'll provide concrete estimates.
05:49 Aisha Kapoor: for annotation we want full outputs not just metrics.
05:53 Priya Nair: we'll include full outputs and annotation exports and per-example confidence where possible.
05:59 Marco Diaz: egress concerns for hosted?
06:02 Jared Morales: hosted endpoints are region-local; we can enable private endpoints or recommend dedicated/private for strict egress policies.
06:11 Samir Patel: timeline for security docs?
06:14 Samir Patel: i'll send SOC2 questionnaire today; expect an answer in 48 hours.
06:20 Jared Morales: noted.
06:23 Jared Morales: recap action items and dates: dataset by 2026-08-04, SOC/KMS list by 2026-07-30, Redwood bench plan by 2026-07-31, bench runs after dataset, review 2026-08-06.
06:40 Evan Cole: we'll also include a sample canary routing rule and fallback policy in the deliverables.
06:45 Hannah Lee: thanks all, excited to see results.
06:48 Jared Morales: thanks, we'll circulate notes and the benchmark plan. meeting adjourned.
